name: Spatial Integration as Determinant of Social Encounter Frequency, Predictability, and Valence
panel_source: SPATIAL-I (Sprint 13.17) — upgrades SC-I structural YAML (Doc 38); this template was already well-calibrated for the encounter-frequency claim (SC-I rated ✓ Good); SPATIAL-I adds the valence-mechanism calibration and working memory interruption parameters

mechanism_chain.description: Spatial integration determines CO-PRESENCE PROBABILITY: in a high-integration space, many movement paths converge, making it probable that any two occupants of a building will pass through the same space simultaneously. Integration is a direct predictor of encounter frequency independent of any other variable.
mechanism_chain.neural_substrate: Environmental property — formal mathematical relationship between integration and co-presence (Hillier & Hanson, 1984)

data.finding: Integration-encounter frequency r = 0.72 — same correlation as integration-movement
data.source: Hillier & Hanson (1984); Space Syntax field studies

data.finding: Co-presence is the necessary condition for social encounter; integration directly predicts co-presence probability
data.effect: Mathematical relationship: integration → co-presence probability → encounter frequency

justification.backing: Encounter frequency is a direct function of co-presence which equals movement co-occurrence. The integration-encounter correlation inherits the meta-analytic level evidence from integration-movement (SC1). This is the strongest empirical claim in SC4.
justification.qualifier: Confidence 0.80 with EMPIRICAL_COVARIANCE — same level as integration-movement. "Among the most replicated Space Syntax findings" (Hillier). Robust across building types and cultures.
justification.rebuttal: The claim would fail if: (a) programmatic factors (office floor assignment, scheduling) dominate encounter frequency over spatial configuration in most buildings — integration predicts potential encounters but organizational structure determines actual encounters.

mechanism_chain.description: ENCOUNTER VALENCE DETERMINATION: The social prediction system evaluates each encounter's CONTEXT to determine valence. Expected encounter in high-integration social space (lobby, break room) → low social PE → social confirmation → positive valence (OFC reward signal). Unexpected encounter in low-integration space (isolated corridor, storage room) → high social PE → amygdala rapid threat appraisal → negative valence until encounter is resolved as safe.
mechanism_chain.neural_substrate: Amygdala rapid person-detection and threat assessment (Whalen, 1998); OFC social reward signal for confirmed positive social predictions; TPJ (temporo-parietal junction) theory of mind for agent prediction during encounter

data.finding: Social prediction system evaluates encounter context: expected = low PE → positive; unexpected = high PE → negative
data.source: Theoretical integration from social neuroscience + spatial analysis
data.effect: Encounter valence determined by prediction match

data.finding: Amygdala rapid person-detection and threat assessment; OFC social reward for confirmed positive predictions
data.effect: Amygdala activated by unexpected person detection; OFC by social reward

justification.backing: The valence determination step connects the frequency claim (Step 1) to the emotional outcome. The mechanism: expected encounters in high-integration social spaces → low social PE → social confirmation → positive valence. Unexpected encounters in low-integration spaces → high social PE → amygdala threat appraisal. Shahar recommended EMPIRICAL_COVARIANCE for SC4 overall "pending a study that independently varies integration and edge condition density."
justification.qualifier: EMPIRICAL_COVARIANCE (Shahar adjudication). The valence mechanism is inferred from social neuroscience literature, not directly tested in architectural encounter studies. The key empirical anchor is Kim & de Dear (2013) — open-plan dissatisfaction. But the specific spatial mechanism (integration × edge condition → predictability → valence) is inferred.
justification.rebuttal: The claim would fail if: (a) encounter valence is determined primarily by social relationship quality (friend vs. stranger) rather than spatial predictability — the same unexpected encounter with a friend may be positive while the same expected encounter with a disliked colleague may be negative, overwhelming the spatial prediction factor.

mechanism_chain.description: OPEN-PLAN CHRONIC MONITORING MECHANISM: High visual integration in open-plan environments produces VISUAL CO-PRESENCE: occupants can see each other continuously. This activates the social prediction system at sub-threshold level continuously — not full social encounter processing, but ambient social monitoring. The mechanism is working memory INTERRUPTION (Meilinger / Salvucci & Taatgen, 2008): peripheral social signals (movement in visual field, raised voice) interrupt the current working memory state at a rate proportional to social density and visual integration. Each interruption requires working memory reconstruction. Over 4+ hours, cumulative working memory interruption costs accumulate as fatigue and dissatisfaction.
mechanism_chain.neural_substrate: DLPFC sustained activation under concurrent task + social monitoring demands; ACC conflict monitoring between current task and social signals; superior temporal sulcus continuous person-motion detection in peripheral visual field; LC arousal burst at each social signal detection

data.finding: Open-plan offices reduce privacy satisfaction and increase noise disturbance, no compensating communication benefit
data.effect: Significant open-plan dissatisfaction across multiple dimensions

data.finding: Working memory INTERRUPTION mechanism: peripheral social signals interrupt WM at rate proportional to social density × visual integration
data.source: Meilinger (panel mechanism); Salvucci & Taatgen (2008) threaded cognition model
data.paradigm: Cognitive interruption model applied to spatial context
data.effect: WM interruption rate ∝ social density × visual integration

justification.backing: Meilinger refined the mechanism: "The social prediction system operates in a PHASIC pattern — attention is captured by social signals and returns to baseline. What differs from private office conditions is the FREQUENCY of capture events, not baseline monitoring level." The mechanism is WM interruption, not sustained monitoring. Shahar endorsed: MECHANISM warrant for the secondary claim (visual co-presence → attention interruption).
justification.qualifier: MECHANISM for the interruption pathway (Shahar adjudication). The chronic monitoring effect accumulates over 4+ hours. Shahar: "chronic social monitoring without edge conditions is an INTEROCEPTIVE load — the sustained prefrontal activation produces arousal signals that IC2 registers as an allostatic cost."
justification.rebuttal: The claim would fail if: (a) open-plan dissatisfaction is primarily about acoustic privacy (noise) rather than visual social monitoring — Kim & de Dear's noise finding may be the primary driver, not spatial configuration; (b) occupant habituation reduces the interruption rate over time — long-term open-plan workers may develop filtering strategies that reduce the PE cost.

mechanism_chain.description: EDGE CONDITION MECHANISM: Edge conditions (Gehl, 1971) — alcoves, window seats, recesses, setbacks from movement paths — give occupants spatial CHOICE over encounter timing. Moving to an edge condition is an AX4 act (taking control of social prediction load). At an edge, the occupant can initiate contact (predictable, chosen → positive social PE) or withdraw (isovist reconfigured to reduce social monitoring demand → load reduction). Buildings without edge conditions eliminate this choice, converting all social co-presence to FORCED encounters.
mechanism_chain.neural_substrate: Prefrontal–amygdala control circuit: edge conditions allow top-down regulation of social threat appraisal; AX4 (perceived control) mediates the valence effect of edge access; oxytocin release in chosen social encounters vs. cortisol in forced social exposure (tentative — no direct architectural measurement)

data.finding: Edge conditions (alcoves, window seats, recesses) give occupants spatial CHOICE over encounter timing
data.effect: Edge access → control over social engagement/withdrawal

data.finding: Moving to edge condition reconfigures isovist to reduce social monitoring demand → load reduction
data.effect: Edge access restores CONTROL over when social capture events occur

justification.backing: Meilinger: "Edge conditions work because they restore CONTROL over when social capture events occur. Moving to an edge is an AX4 act." The mechanism connects to AX4 (perceived control) and IC2 (allostatic cost reduction). Buildings without edge conditions convert all co-presence to forced encounters.
justification.qualifier: Confidence moderate. The edge condition concept is well-established in architectural theory (Gehl 1971) but the specific mechanism (AX4-mediated working memory load control) is Meilinger's panel contribution, not independently validated.
justification.rebuttal: The claim would fail if: (a) edge conditions are primarily about physical comfort (leaning, sitting) rather than social control — the benefit may be postural, not social-predictive; (b) in cultures with different social norms, edge conditions may not provide the assumed control over encounters.

spatial_configuration.construct: Rate of working memory interruptions per hour attributable to social signal detection in open-plan vs. enclosed-office conditions
spatial_configuration.unit: interruptions per hour above enclosed-office baseline
spatial_configuration.flag: THEORETICAL_DEFAULT — no direct architectural measurement of interruption rate; extrapolated from general interruption literature (Czerwinski et al., 2004) + Kim and de Dear (2013) noise disturbance data
spatial_configuration.mechanism_note: Salvucci & Taatgen (2008) threaded cognition: each interruption requires 7–25 seconds of working memory reconstruction (varies by task type and interruption depth). At 4 interruptions/hour = 30–100 seconds/hour of reconstruction cost, compounding over 8-hour workday.

acoustic_masking_system.rationale: Acoustic masking reduces the salience of peripheral social signals; Kim and de Dear (2013) identify noise as primary driver of open-plan dissatisfaction

visual_screen_height_above_1.2m.rationale: Screens reduce visual co-presence while maintaining spatial integration; visual interruption rate falls; acoustic interruption rate unchanged

workstation_density_above_10_per_100m2.rationale: Density amplifies both visual and acoustic social signal rate; Kim and de Dear: crowding compounds noise and lack of privacy effects

architectural_threshold.construct: Effect of edge condition provision (alcoves, setbacks, window seats per 10m of corridor) on self-reported social interaction quality
architectural_threshold.central_estimate: +0.8 to +1.2 points on 7-point social satisfaction scale
architectural_threshold.flag: THEORETICAL_DEFAULT — Gehl observational data on public space + Whyte's 'The Social Life of Small Urban Spaces'; direct controlled measurement in building interiors absent
architectural_threshold.note: Total encounter quantity increases modestly with edge conditions; encounter QUALITY (duration, depth, willingness to linger) increases substantially — edge conditions convert social PE from forced-unpredictable to chosen-predictable

environmental_novelty_level.construct: GSR elevation at unexpected person encounter in low-integration space vs. expected encounter in high-integration space
environmental_novelty_level.flag: THEORETICAL_DEFAULT — extrapolated from general social-surprise literature (Herry et al., 2010); no direct architectural measurement
environmental_novelty_level.note: Resolves quickly (3–10 seconds) once the encounter is appraised as non-threatening; sustained only if the low-integration spatial context maintains persistent threat uncertainty

ie_dpt_interaction.implicit: T_IE_007 (Spatial Safety Monitoring) — the implicit channel continuously evaluates social configuration for threat: who is here, how many, are any in the low-integration spaces where unexpected encounter is most threatening
ie_dpt_interaction.explicit: T_IE_006 (Social Norm Evaluation) — the explicit channel monitors whether social behavior in the space conforms to normative expectations; Kirsh's explicit sense applies — occupants can deliberately modulate their social monitoring strategy (headphones in open plan = explicit choice to reduce implicit monitoring load)

primary: Offices — especially open-plan (SC4 is the template most directly implicated)
Universities and schools (corridor encounter ecology; classroom visual integration)
Healthcare (patient-staff encounter patterns; staff social load in nursing stations)
secondary: Cultural buildings (planned social encounter in foyers, galleries)
low_applicability: Solitary occupancy buildings (private residences without shared spaces)

key_references: Hillier, B., & Hanson, J. (1984). The social logic of space. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511597237
Kim, J., & de Dear, R. (2013). Workspace satisfaction: The privacy-communication trade-off in open-plan offices. Journal of Environmental Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvp.2013.06.007

Salvucci, D. D., & Taatgen, N. A. (2008). Threaded cognition. Psychological Review. https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-295X.115.1.101

panel_reasoning_excerpt:
### Template SC4: Spatial Configuration and Social Encounter Prediction

```yaml
template_id: "SPATIAL_SOCIAL_ENCOUNTER_001"
display_id: "SC4"
name: "Spatial Configuration as Determinant of Social Encounter Frequency and Quality"

structural_pattern: >
  Spatial configuration creates the conditions for social encounter
  by determining WHO encounters WHOM, HOW OFTEN, and in WHAT CONTEXT.
  Space Syntax integration predicts not only individual movement but
  the CO-PRESENCE of multiple individuals: high-integration spaces
  are where paths converge, making encounter likely. The frequency
  of social encounters is a direct function of spatial integration.
  
  Social encounters are PE events: encountering another person means
  encountering an agent whose behavior must be predicted (T48–T52
  social brain templates). The VALENCE of social encounter PE depends
  on the spatial context:
  
  EXPECTED ENCOUNTERS in high-integration social spaces (office
  break room, village square, building lobby) → low social PE →
  social confirmation → pleasant, bonding.
  
  UNEXPECTED ENCOUNTERS in low-integration spaces (hospital
  corridor at night, parking garage, dead-end) → high social PE
  → T5 threat assessment → anxiety until the encounter is
  resolved as safe.
  
  Spatial configuration also determines VISUAL ACCESS between
  people (who can see whom), which affects social monitoring,
  perceived privacy, and the sense of being observed. High visual
  connectivity (open plan, transparent partitions) → constant
  social monitoring → social prediction system always active →
  social PE load may accumulate over extended occupancy.
  Low visual connectivity (private offices, acoustic/visual
  separation) → infrequent social encounters → low social PE
  load but also reduced social reward.
  
  Edge conditions (Gehl) — the boundaries between public
  movement paths and semi-private stationary zones — are the
  spatial features that create OPTIONAL social encounter:
  places where a person can choose to engage or withdraw.
  Buildings that provide rich edge conditions support social
  choice; buildings without edges force either constant
  exposure (open plan) or complete isolation (private cells).

higher_order_principle: >
  The social dimension of spatial prediction. As SC1 describes
  how spatial configuration determines NAVIGATIONAL prediction,
  SC4 describes how spatial configuration determines SOCIAL
  prediction: the probability, context, and valence of
  encountering other people. The social prediction is layered
  on the spatial prediction — you must be in a space to
  encounter someone there, so the spatial network determines
  the distribution of social PE events across the building.
  
  Open-plan offices are the canonical negative case: they
  maximize visual co-presence (constant social monitoring)
  while eliminating edges (no withdrawal option), producing
  chronic elevated social PE that manifests as distraction,
  reduced deep work, and paradoxically reduced meaningful
  social interaction (because people withdraw into
  headphones and screens to escape the uncontrolled
  social prediction load).

IC2_body_budget.interaction: SC4 feeds IC2 as one of the most chronic architectural stressors in contemporary building types. Open-plan office occupants spending 8 hours/day in high-visual-integration environments accumulate a daily allostatic load from social monitoring demands that IC2 registers as elevated body budget expenditure. Kim and de Dear (2013) document the outcome: 90% of open-plan workers report noise and lack of privacy as their primary workplace complaint, even when they report general job satisfaction. The IC2 mechanism explains why: the allostatic cost of chronic social monitoring is real even when consciously tolerated.
IC2_body_budget.direction: SC4 feeds IC2 chronically for prolonged open-plan occupancy; effect compounds with SC2 (small isovist) and T14 (navigational stress) in high-density workplaces

AX4_perceived_control.interaction: SC4 is perhaps the most direct architectural determinant of AX4 in workplace and educational settings. The CHOICE over social encounter timing — determined by edge condition availability — IS perceived social control. Removing edge conditions removes the spatial mechanism of social agency. This is why open-plan offices have such strongly negative AX4 scores despite ostensibly 'collaborative' intentions: the design removes the spatial prerequisite for social self-determination.
AX4_perceived_control.direction: Edge condition density feeds AX4 directly; visual integration (without edge conditions) feeds AX4 inversely

higher_order_principle: →  pathway: The mechanism by which spatial integration as determinant of social encounter frequency, predictability, and valence operates
